correctness.rationale: The Hilbert quadrilateral identity on every rook rectangle proves squared distortion at least 2 and U+V>=4. With squared rook diagonal distances >=4, variance around the rook centroid A=[(M-1)U+(N-1)V+(M-1)(N-1)W]/(2MN) and hub variance B>=(h-1)/(2h) give the sharp second bound D^2(2MN+M-N)>=4N(M-1)+MN(1-1/h); no equivariance is assumed for the lower bound. Three centered mutually orthogonal regular simplices with coordinate squared lengths (2,2), or (4-L,L) in the binding regime, attain every bound. Equality implies zero rectangle defects, additive coordinate splitting, orthogonality and regular-simplex rigidity at and above L=2; translation of the hub simplex in a new orthogonal direction gives continuum below L=2. No source-formula corrections were required: all m,n>=2,h>=1 and equal-threshold cases are covered. This analytic proof is independent of finite checking.

Exact classification of all labelled optimal embeddings in binding cases is nontrivial geometric information, not a routine specialization of Hamming graph distortion.

limitations: Only simple unweighted K_h join (K_m square K_n), m,n>=2,h>=1 and real Hilbert targets; no complete classification of subthreshold optimal embeddings.
